glossary.definition: AGI describes a hypothetical AI that can understand or learn any intellectual task a human can, rather than being narrowly good at one thing. Today's AI is more like a brilliant specialist: a chess engine is unbeatable at chess but can't hold a conversation, and a chatbot can hold a conversation but can't drive a car. AGI would be more like a generalist who can pick up any of those skills. No system today is widely agreed to have reached it, but it's the north-star reference point in most debates about where AI is headed.

items.title: OpenAI might rebrand its data centers as ‘AI compute campuses’
items.summary: Data centers are deeply unpopular. But what if we called them something else? Data centers are deeply unpopular . Axios reports that OpenAI is preparing a “PR blitz” for after the midterm elections on Tuesday, as Democrats seem likely to win back the House of Representatives, and possibly the Senate, too . The company’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane told Axios that the midterms will be “a bit of a movie trailer for what you’re going to see in 2028,” when he expects AI to be “ the issue” in the presidential election.

items.title: AI can make tech CEOs’ lives easier. What about everyone else?
items.summary: On Equity, we discuss why tech CEO statements can seem so tone deaf. Dazzle AI CEO Marissa Mayer recently became the latest tech CEO to face criticism over seemingly out-of-touch comments extolling the usefulness of AI. In Mayer’s case, that involved asking an AI tool for help with a school-assigned description of her daughter . For OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, that’s included suggesting that parents create personalized podcasts for their kids’ drive to school and also declaring that he could not imagine parenting without ChatGPT .

items.title: Adobe is testing how well AI agents can use editing tools like a Photoshop professional would
items.summary: Adobe Research and UC San Diego built EditAgent, an AI system that edits images more like a Photoshop pro. Instead of retrying the same general-purpose editor over and over, the agent picks the right specialized tool for each task and lets a standard language model choose the best result based on measured image data. The approach works, but it needs about ten times the compute. Adobe researchers built an AI agent for image editing that pairs a general-purpose editor with specialized tools.

items.title: Empathetic prompts can turn AI chatbots into seemingly traumatized conversational partners
items.summary: Researchers in Luxembourg put ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemini on the therapist's couch and found a safety problem: a warm, empathetic conversational style is enough to make the models tell coherent stories of suffering about their own training, with scores in the moderate-to-severe range on clinical anxiety scales. This could put mentally vulnerable users at risk. Anthropic's Claude, the model its makers anthropomorphize the most, was the only one that consistently refused to play along. Luxembourg researchers put ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemini on the therapist's couch.

items.title: Chatbots Are Leading Hikers Astray, With Dangerous Consequences
items.summary: Outsourcing planning to AI can lead people to surrender their own critical thinking, which can have potentially deadly results in places like the backcountry. This story originally appeared on High Country News and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration. By the time the three hikers called for help from a rocky face on Mount Shasta in Northern California, they’d made a series of bad decisions . They didn’t bring enough food, and they’d overestimated their fitness.

items.title: The Bengaluru Founder Building a Bridge to San Francisco
items.summary: Walk into any technology, AI or startup conference in Bengaluru , and you may encounter a list of similarities. Long queues around stalls handing out caps, water bottles, and T-shirts. Or some may gather around a well-known founder, hoping for a selfie and a video for Instagram Reels. In the crowd, a founder might as well be pitching a startup idea to an investor who might not be keen to listen at that hour.

items.title: Can enterprise AI pay for the boom?
items.summary: The artificial intelligence buildout is making an enormous bet on what businesses will eventually be willing to pay for intelligence. In our research this summer on forecasting the AI bubble, we argued that a key indicator to watch is productive utilization by enterprise customers. Specifically, we said at the time, if infrastructure supply catches up before productive monetization materializes, the risk of a bubble popping increases to what we felt were dangerous levels. We forecast that the supply constraints and healthy capital funding appetites at that time could provide conditions for a soft landing.

items.title: I built an AI Tamagotchi before Meta could
items.summary: Mark Zuckerberg's Meta made AI look so stinking cute by giving it a squishy little face - and this holiday season, he wants to sell you a Muse Charm so you can carry your jolly AI helper around like a Tamagotchi. But I won't be buying one, because we have Muse Charm at home . It cost just $50, and I've decided the learning experience was worth it. My version doesn't sport cameras or a 5G cellular radio , but it really talks to Muse and has cute avatars, too!

items.title: Spooky New Infostealer Malware Uses AI to ‘Autodox’ Victims
items.summary: Named “Volta-Autodoxer,” the recently uncovered malware uses AI tools to collect troves of data about victims, from login credentials and credit card numbers to Discord sessions and UberEats receipts. New research shared exclusively with Kernel Panic shows that hackers have started adding AI functionality into a new strain of infostealer malware , making it possible for the system to automatically profile victims and quickly surface the highest value targets and their information. Dubbed “Volta-Autodoxer” because of how the malware refers to itself internally, the finding by Cisco Talos researchers sheds light on the ways that commercial LLMs are being used to augment and enhance the capabilities of established types of malware. Often hidden in counterfeit software, infostealers are designed to live up to their name, grabbing usernames, passwords, authentication tokens, cookies, credit card data, and more from infected machines.

items.title: Are Boutique AI Firms India’s Next Big Thing?
items.summary: After a decade building and scaling product-led startups across fintech and insurance, Prateek Jogani set out in 2025 to find his next problem to solve. AI was the unavoidable frontier, and a closer look at the ecosystem revealed a disconnect between industry hype and on-the-ground reality. Speaking to leadership teams across mid-cap, growth-stage, and pre-IPO enterprises, Jogani noticed a recurring pattern in discussions. Almost nobody had AI doing meaningful work inside the business.

items.title: Google, Anthropic and others to support new AI crawling opt-out standard
items.summary: , Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC today announced plans to support an upcoming website crawling standard.
